reasons: Section 2.2 plainly imposes a sole-and-exclusive supplier obligation on Customer for the whole term with no product-category limit, no 12-month cap and no performance-based exit — squarely walk-away territory under EXCLUSIVITY, so the 'deviation' status is correct and the clause does not meet the fallback.

The redline removes the exclusivity ('sole and exclusive provider' → 'a provider') and affirms freedom to source from third parties, reaching the preferred position; the deterministic check confirms no requirements/sole-supplier obligation on Customer remains.
The high changed-character ratio (0.761) is justified here: the rule requires excising the operative exclusivity commitment, which cannot be done without rewriting the short sentence.

The comment is accurate, correctly cites the playbook position and the internal conflict with Section 12.3 (which lacks an order-of-precedence override), and the rationale properly offers the fallback if Vendor pushes back.

Minor note only: the added 'no obligation to purchase any minimum volume' sentence goes slightly beyond what EXCLUSIVITY strictly requires and duplicates Section 12.3; it is harmless and consistent with our position, but the leaner edit would stop at removing exclusivity.
